selected_branches.branch: Pedestrian permission paired with a separate driver duty.

law_text: Except as otherwise provided in NRS 484B.287 [NRS-484B-287-1c, NRS-484B-287-1d, NRS-484B-287-1e, LVMC-11-30-060-A, LVMC-11-30-060-B], 484B.290 [LVMC-11-30-140-B] and 484B.350 [LVMC-11-46-030]: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows: While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal and must be given the right-of-way by the drivers of all vehicles.

witness_review.branch: Pedestrian permission paired with a separate driver duty.
required_context: Establish pedestrian classification, highway dedication and public access, signal identity, facing direction and illuminated Walk interval.
Establish pedestrian ego classification and crossing route separately from longitudinal vehicle travel.
Identify a separate qualifying vehicle and driver for the active right-of-way interaction.
Identify the separate vehicle and driver and retain their motion relative to pedestrian ego.
Preserve introductory exceptions and unresolved right-of-way judgments; the pedestrian is the permission holder rather than the driver-duty subject.
Preserve one-way geometry and distinguish the pedestrian crossing route from longitudinal vehicle travel.
Provide a facing illuminated Walk or walking person symbol indicating ego's crossing direction.
Record governing signals and investigate the introductory exceptions.
Retain one-way geometry and establish highway dedication, public access and extent.
witness_review.reason: Pedestrian ego can travel across the fixed one-way road at the crosswalk under a facing Walk signal.
